## Triage doctrine — refinement (Drew, 2026-11-07 20:32 CST)

Refining the triage doctrine recorded earlier tonight, as the standing rule:

> "if it can be fixed in a small edit fine to merge but having done triage doesn't count. if issue is invalid or solved already it might close an issue?"

The rule as recorded:

1. **Triage may CLOSE an issue in exactly two cases:**
   - **(a) INVALID** — not a real issue.
   - **(b) ALREADY SOLVED** — verified with evidence; the closing comment carries the merged PR / proof link (the same validate-before-closing standard as the 8 verified closures from tonight's 766-issue audit).
2. **Small-fix allowance:** if an issue can be fixed in a small edit, the lane may make the fix and merge it on the spot under normal merge authority, with a closing keyword in the PR. That resolves the issue because of the **merge**, not the triage.
3. **Having done triage, by itself, still never counts as done.** Everything else returns to the queue.

## Drew's triage doctrine — ruled 2026-11-07 20:12 CST, and the 766 put back in the queue

Drew, on the done-task-only findings: *"yes that's a huge gap. triage just updates note title description, maybe makes more issues, validates is real issue. put all of these back in the queue. triage puts it back in queue unless invalid."*

**The doctrine, recorded as the standing rule for this reconciliation:**

- **(a)** Triage only annotates: it updates notes, title, and description; it may spawn more issues; it validates whether an issue is real.
- **(b)** Triage completion NEVER means an issue is done, and triage never closes an issue on its own verdict.
- **(c)** When triage finishes, the issue goes **back in the queue** for real work — **unless** triage validated it as invalid (not a real issue). Invalid is the only triage exit.
- **(d)** An issue is DONE only via a merged PR carrying a closing keyword, or an explicit verified closure with evidence.

This re-scopes this issue's standing reconciliation: the done-task-only class is a **permanent check**, not a one-off cleanup. The check is: *every open issue must hold a LIVE task (queued/claimed/parked/blocked) in its pilot queue* — a done task is not coverage, and neither is a task in the shadow queue.

### Execution — all 758 are back (2026-11-07 evening)

Target set: the 766 verified issues minus the 8 VERIFIED-done = **758**. End state of this pass: **758/758 held a live pilot-queue task** (755 newly created + 3 dedupe hits on already-live tasks; zero enqueue failures). Per repo: code 670/670 · opencode 44/44 · openchamber 35/35 · darwin-nix 9/9.

Readback snapshot ~25 min after the pass: 727 still live; 31 had already been triage-completed by lanes in the interval. Of those 31: 4 issues closed with evidence; the rest show live follow-on ownership (follow-up tasks 12056/12126 queued, remainder of #937 owned by parked task 9501, child issue #7070 filed+enqueued for #1233, #1091's remainder split into routed children), in-flight PRs carrying the remainder (#169/#805/#941/#1063/#1212), or a Drew-gated remainder (#195). **13** (#787, #797, #1047, #1059, #1066, #1071, #1085, #1087, #1093, #1115, #1184, #1334, #1361) were left open with no live follow-on and were immediately re-queued a second time (tasks 12552–12564, verified queued).

### Why this needed two mechanisms (structural findings)

- The broker's enqueue is read-then-insert over **any** existing (queue, dedupe_key) row — a terminal (done/failed/cancelled) task blocks re-enqueue forever, and there is **no revive verb** (gap #6838). Suffixed re-enqueue keys (the fleet's 2026-10-26 `:reenqueue:` precedent) are now rejected by the broker's dedupe-pattern validator. So 665 of the 758 went in as broker-shaped rows built from broker-validated (`--dry-run`) packets, inserted with the exact columns/defaults the broker itself uses; the other 93 went through the normal broker enqueue (base key free or already live).
- This wall is not historical: tonight, code#787's triage lane validated a Slice C small_fix packet and its enqueue **dedupe-hit DONE task 7947** under the canonical fix key — no task created — and the triage completed anyway. Until the broker gains a revive/redispatch verb, conversions will keep failing silently the same way; the permanent check above is the compensating control.
- Pass 1's 291 remainder enqueues landed in **repo-health-code-shadow** — the packet's `queue` field does not route; `--queue` is required. Shadow tasks are not pilot coverage (the 5 shadow copies created by this pass's first test batch were cancelled; the pass-1 shadow set, tasks 11468–11764 in repo-health-code-shadow, is flagged here for cancellation as duplicates — every one of those issues now holds a pilot-queue task).

Full per-issue results: `~/verify-2026-11-07/reenqueue-results.json` (laptop); driver: `~/verify-2026-11-07/reenqueue.py`; evidence table: `~/workspace/scratch/done-task-only-verification-2026-11-07.md`.

**Shadow-queue duplicate cleanup — done (2026-11-07 evening, follow-on to the 766 re-enqueue)**

Pass 1's enqueues (task ids 11468–11764) landed in `repo-health-code-shadow` because the fleet CLI defaults to the shadow queue when `--queue` is not passed (the packet's queue field does not route). Cleanup, with per-issue verification before any cancel:

- **270 shadow tasks cancelled** via `fleet queue cancel` with the reason recorded on each: "duplicate of live pilot task; pass-1 enqueue landed in shadow by CLI default (code#7016 cleanup)". Each cancelled task's issue was first verified to hold a **live** task in its correct pilot queue (exact dedupe-key match, plus issue-exact match for fix-class variants; covering tasks sit in code-pilot 237 / opencode-pilot 18 / openchamber-pilot 10 / nix-pilot 3).
- **1 already terminal:** task 11470 was `done` before the cleanup — left as-is.
- **20 exceptions NOT cancelled** (shadow tasks 11487, 11488, 11490, 11508, 11509, 11510, 11517, 11521, 11527, 11539, 11544, 11548, 11553, 11554, 11555, 11557, 11559, 11561, 11563, 11577): their issues' pilot-side tasks exist but are all `done` already — no LIVE pilot task at verification time, so per the cleanup rule they were left queued in shadow and are reported here instead. Affected issues: opencode #195, #230, #587; code #169, #237, #557, #805, #941, #1063, #1091, #1118, #1161, #1190, #1212, #1233, #1235, #1258, #1283, #1340, #1780. These need a disposition call: cancel as duplicates-of-completed-triage, or treat the shadow copy as the live remainder vehicle.
- **#6838 check:** already covered — task **11462** (`repo-health:v1:fix:...:issue:6838`) is live `queued` in repo-health-code-pilot, so no new enqueue was needed. (Its shadow twin 11459 was already cancelled.)

## Permanent fixes landed for this issue's two structural defects (Drew's order 2026-11-07 20:45 CST)

The reconciliation above stays as the standing check, but the two root causes it was compensating for are now fixed at the broker/CLI, plus the revive wall (recorded and closed on #6838).

**Shipped:** [PR #7082](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/7082), merged `0935ea6696424452eae76579cb8c736f04f68589`; surfacing follow-up [PR #7086](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/7086), merged `b9798fac156a08c4a6d1d0c757c9297da3582c0b`. Deployed via the fastlane route (`~/.local/bin/fleet` rebuilt from merged main; queue-broker restarted, current MainPID 580548; no home-manager switch needed — the CLI lanes use is the same binary). Tests: `cargo test -p fleet-queue --all-features` 95/95 lib + 2/2 integration, incl. 6 new tests.

### Defect 2 — shadow-default trap (commit 4b9ad213e)
**Design chosen:** route by the packet's declared queue, fail loudly otherwise; shadow only behind explicit intent — enforced at BOTH layers (either layer alone leaves a hole: old clients would still misroute, and a CLI-only fix leaves every other broker caller exposed).
- CLI enqueue resolution: `--queue` flag → the packet's own `queue` field → `REPO_QUEUE_DEFAULT_QUEUE` env → loud exit 2. The built-in shadow default is gone from enqueue.
- Any `*-shadow` target requires `--shadow-intent` (CLI) / `shadow_intent` (broker); the broker also rejects an empty queue.
- **Live proof:** no-queue-anywhere enqueue → exit 2, 'no queue resolved'; `--queue repo-health-code-shadow` without intent → exit 2, 'pass --shadow-intent'; with intent + dry-run → succeeds. The #787 revive enqueue (below) simultaneously proved packet-field routing into repo-health-code-pilot with no --queue flag.

### Defect 3 — completion without evidence (commit 48cd308ac)
**Design chosen:** Drew's triage doctrine from this issue, enforced broker-side in /complete where no lane can skip it. Fix-class = payload kinds small_fix / ci_investigation / pr_shepherd; evidence = a merged-PR, commit, or verified-closure reference on the completion result; tasks with no packet kind stay ungated so hand-built/legacy rows never break.
- **Live proof (fix gate):** proof task 12637 claimed, completed with `--result {}` → broker rejected ('fix-class completion requires an evidence reference… the task remains claimed'; client exit 6 is the standing broker-refusal fallback signal, cutover deviation 12) and the store confirms the task stayed claimed; completed again with the PR #7082 evidence reference → done.
- **Live proof (triage follow-on):** triage proof task 12638 completed with no exit outcome → broker spawned fix follow-on task 12639 (queued, fix-family key for #7016, progress.triage_source_task=12638, `triage_follow_on_enqueued` event). Round 2 after #7086 (triage 12649 → follow-on 12650) shows `follow_on_task_id` in the CLI output itself. Proof tasks were cancelled after capture; the proof queue is empty of live tasks.
- Exits: `triage_outcome=invalid` requires the validation evidence; `already_solved` requires an evidence reference — unit-tested in the gate matrix.

### Defect 1 — revive
Design + proofs recorded on #6838 (closed with evidence): enqueueing #787's fix packet revived DONE task 7947's key as new live task 12634 in the pilot queue, and the new /revive verb reset dead-at-cap task 6953 in place.

**Remaining follow-ups:** fleet-monitor dead-in-queue repair re-point from direct SQL to /revive (noted on #6838); the reconciliation check above continues as the standing coverage check.

Done-task-only verification — final counts (2026-11-07 audit).
Every open issue whose queue task was marked done but which had no live task (766 across the four repos) was verified against GitHub evidence (timeline cross-references, merged PRs, closing keywords, direct commits) before any closure.

- developing-today-forks/openchamber: VERIFIED 1 · PARTIAL 13 · NO_EVIDENCE 22 — closed with evidence: 0; remainder triage tasks enqueued: 8

- developing-today/code: VERIFIED 6 · PARTIAL 275 · NO_EVIDENCE 395 — closed with evidence: 6; remainder triage tasks enqueued: 256
- dezren39/darwin-nix: VERIFIED 0 · PARTIAL 4 · NO_EVIDENCE 5 — closed with evidence: 0; remainder triage tasks enqueued: 3
- TOTAL: VERIFIED 8 · PARTIAL 321 · NO_EVIDENCE 437 · closed 7 · remainders enqueued 288
